myths.title: Name and Meaning
myths.text: The name means "He who goes forth shining; the Nahuatl sun god" and reflects the figure's role in the tradition.

lore.syncretism: Tōnatiuh appears within the Nahuatl tradition and has influenced later retellings, artistic depictions, and scholarly study. The Unicode restoration preserves the name's distinctive orthography for contemporary use.
lore.culturalLegacy: Tōnatiuh continues to appear in scholarship, art, and popular reception as a significant figure of the Nahuatl tradition. Restoring the name in Unicode returns the original marks that ASCII removes.
lore.extendedMeditation: Tōnatiuh embodies sun, heat, fifth age in the Nahuatl imagination. The name's restoration is not merely cosmetic: it recovers the stress, length, and script that make the figure recognizable in the source tradition.
lore.archaeology: Tōnatiuh is attested in the textual and iconographic record of the Nahuatl tradition.
